title: PPSSPP adapts to Android's modern storage model
summary: PPSSPP documents folder selection and scoped storage so game libraries remain accessible without broad legacy filesystem permissions.
heroAlt: PPSSPP adapts to Android's modern storage model
searchKeywords: PPSSPP adapts to Android's modern storage model

blocks.text: Scoped storage replaces broad disk access

Modern Android asks the user to grant PPSSPP access to a chosen directory through the system document picker. The resulting permission is narrower than legacy whole-storage access and can survive restarts when the platform grants persistent access.
The folder becomes a library root

PPSSPP remembers the selected location for browsing game images and related files. It does not need to copy an entire library into private application storage, but it must use Android's document APIs when ordinary filesystem paths are unavailable.

PSP savedata, states and configuration must remain writable even when game images are read from a protected or removable location. PPSSPP separates emulator-owned data from library access so revoking one folder does not silently destroy progress.
Picker failures are not game failures

A directory can be unavailable because permission was revoked, the provider changed or Android refuses selection of a protected root. The official storage guides isolate those cases before a missing ISO is misreported as an emulation or compatibility regression.
Moving a library is an explicit operation

PPSSPP documents how to select a new location and preserve files. Treating that transition as host storage work keeps PSP paths and game identifiers stable while Android changes the URI used to reach the underlying documents. For a clean migration, users should identify the current PSP folder before changing access, copy or move it with a tool that can see both locations, and then grant PPSSPP the destination directory through Android's picker. Verifying a known save and one game image immediately catches a permission mistake. This sequence avoids confusing a revoked document-tree grant with deleted data and keeps backup decisions separate from emulator configuration.
